title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes Grothendieck studies 2-dimensional linear data. A pair (ρ,σ) of 2x2 matrices plays the role of the images of the canonical loops/generators (ρ of 'order 3', σ of 'order 2' up to scalars). M_{ρ,σ} is an algebraic group of symmetries of such a solution of the loop equations, a sort of linear analogue of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group attached to (ρ,σ). From the previous pages it has a subgroup M_{ρ,σ}(0) (the part fixing the base point / 'inertia' part) and a half-direct (semidirect) decomposition M_{ρ,σ} = M_{ρ,σ}(0)·S^+_{ρ,σ}, with S^+_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG ≅ Ĝ^+_{ρ,σ}. There is a canonical map M_{ρ,σ} → τ_{ρ,σ}, where τ_{ρ,σ} is a group built from the centralizer tori T_ρ, T_σ ⊂ GL_2.

This page records the bookkeeping of canonical subgroups.

(39) Neutral components: 1 → M° → M → μ_2×μ_2 → 1. The component group is detected by two sign characters ε_2, ε_3. M° itself is the semidirect product M°(0)·S^+.

(40) M(0)° ≅ τ° ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ. This is the fibre product of the two 2-dimensional maximal tori over the determinant: pairs of elements with equal determinant, a 3-dimensional torus.

(41) M° is the inverse image of τ° under the canonical map M → τ.

(42) The composite M → τ → G_m is a character χ. On τ° it is the common determinant.

(43) This gives two exact sequences:
- 1 → M^+ → M → G_m → 1,
- 1 → M°+ → M° → G_m → 1.

(44) These kernels again split as semidirect products:
- M^+ ≅ M^+(0)·S^+, with M^+(0) ≅ τ^+;
- M°+ ≅ M°+(0)·S^+, with M°+(0) ≅ τ°+ ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ (cf. (28)).

(45) M°+(0) := Ker(M(0) → G_m×μ_2×μ_2 via (χ,ε_2,ε_3)) ≅ ST_ρ×ST_σ. Here ST denotes the determinant-1 part of the torus; dimension 2 = 3 − 1, which is consistent.

Key claim. This 2-dimensional torus ST_ρ×ST_σ is central in M° but not in M. The next page makes this precise: it computes subgroups of the centre and specializes to the 'modular case'. That case is det ρ = det σ = 1, i.e. ρ, σ the standard order-6 and order-4 generators of SL_2(Z), so that ρ itself lies in the centre of M°.

Purpose. Determine the structure (components, characters, tori, centre) of the symmetry group of a rank-2 linear solution of the loop equations. This is groundwork for comparing the profinite/arithmetic situation (Ĝ_{0,3}, GT-type actions) with the linear, modular SL_2 situation.
errors: (45): the kernel is written as taken inside M°(0) while including the sign characters ε_2, ε_3, which are trivial on a connected group. Presumably M(0) (or M(0)° with ε's redundant) is intended; harmless.

The decomposition labels in (44) (τ^+ vs τ°+) are slightly loose: identifying M^+(0) with τ^+ requires M(0) → τ to be an isomorphism, which is asserted only for neutral components in (40). This is an unstated assumption rather than a demonstrated error.

The claim that ST_ρ×ST_σ is central in M° requires S^+ (the 'SG' part) to commute with M°+(0). This is asserted, not proved, on this page; the next page's margin warns that everything should be redone 'modulo radicaux'.

ideas.what: Structure of the symmetry group M_{ρ,σ} of a 2-dimensional linear solution of the loop equations: component group μ2×μ2, neutral component = torus·S^+ (semidirect)
ideas.modern_name: Linear (GL_2) analogue of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type automorphism group; component group / Levi-type decomposition of an algebraic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct published analogue known; linear GT-type questions appear in Ihara, Drinfeld, Hain–Matsumoto in other forms

ideas.what: M(0)° ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ (fibre product of the two centralizer tori over det), with character χ = det and kernel ST_ρ×ST_σ
ideas.modern_name: Fibre product of maximal tori over the determinant; norm-one tori

ideas.what: Centrality of ST_ρ×ST_σ in the neutral component but not in the whole group; modular case det ρ = det σ = 1 corresponding to SL_2(Z) generators
ideas.modern_name: Centre computation of a non-connected algebraic group; modular (SL_2(Z)) specialization of B_3-type representations

missed.claim: Grothendieck lists canonical subgroups (M°, M^+, M°+, τ°, τ^+, τ°+) 'to compute' and asserts a semidirect structure and partial centre of the symmetry group of rank-2 solutions of the loop equations. The full program of describing these groups, and comparing them with GT-type profinite symmetries, is not in the literature as such.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Rank-2 linear representations of braid/mapping-class (Teichmüller) towers and their symmetry groups touch on motivic Galois actions in low rank. Still, the page itself is routine algebraic-group bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine structural bookkeeping (components, characters, tori, centres) of an algebraic symmetry group in Grothendieck's unpublished linear study of the loop equations. It is interesting as documentation of that program, but contains no result a specialist would find new or deep.
transcription_corrections: The circled '(30)' at the top left is a margin/section marker, not an equation number.
First line likely reads: 'On désigne par M°_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ}[0]°, M_{ρ,σ}(0)° les composantes neutres'. The crossed-out third item is probably M_{ρ,σ}(0)° rather than a repeat of [0]°.
Margin note likely lists 'M°_{ρσ}, M^+_{ρσ}, M^{+°}_{ρσ}, τ°_{ρσ}, τ^+_{ρσ}, τ^{°+}_{ρσ} ... quelques sous-groupes canoniques à calculer ...'; the ending is uncertain.
After (42): 'également noté χ, dont le noyau sera noté M^+_{ρ,σ}, et le noyau de χ sur M°_{ρ,σ}, M°+_{ρ,σ}, d'où'.
